result.summary:
Read every one of MOBILE-DEV's 8 test files (apps/mobile/test/{guards,security,auth,bootstrap,design_system}/) plus the guard's target source files (lib/auth/auth.dart, lib/api/api_client.dart, lib/api/transport_policy.dart, lib/bootstrap/navigation_bootstrap.dart, lib/design_system/masked_text.dart, android/app/src/{main,debug}/..., ios/Runner/Info.plist, docs/mobile/architecture.md, pubspec.yaml) directly rather than trusting MOBILE-DEV's handoff summary alone. Decomposed AC1-AC9 into the clauses listed in this step's dispatch and mapped each to a specific test:testname in test/specs/REQ-422.md's coverage table.

ONE REAL GAP FOUND AND CLOSED (AC1/clause 1b): apps/mobile/test/guards/token_storage_boundary_guard_test.dart had self-tests proving the checker's flutter_secure_storage-import branch and dart:io-File(...) branch each fire on a violating fixture, but NO self-test for the shared_preferences-import branch -- the real-tree assertion passes only because shared_preferences isn't a pubspec dependency at all (confirmed absent), which proves nothing about whether that specific regex/scoping logic in the checker itself works. Added two tests: 'self-test: checker fires on a fixture importing shared_preferences under lib/auth/' (proves the detection fires) and 'self-test: a shared_preferences import OUTSIDE lib/auth/ or lib/api/ fires zero violations (boundary is scoped, not global)' (proves the scoping is to lib/auth/+lib/api/, not global -- otherwise 'no file under lib/auth/ or lib/api/' would be indistinguishable from a checker that just flags shared_preferences everywhere).

All other clauses (AC1 1a/1c/1d; AC2 2a/2b/2c; AC3 3a-3e; AC5 5a-5f; AC6 6a/6b; AC7 7a/7b; AC8 8a/8b/8c) already had a test whose failure would be caused specifically by that clause's violation -- verified by reading each assertion, not by test/testWidgets name matching alone. AC8/clause 8c (flagged in the dispatch as 'most likely to be missing') is in fact well covered: the widget test explicitly attempts a second reveal via a direct controller.reveal() call (bypassing the UI in case the icon becomes absent once locked) and asserts the phase stays locked and the real value stays hidden, plus a separate controller-only test asserting reveal()/hide() are no-ops (don't notify listeners) once locked.

AC4 (command-execution): re-read handoffs/WF02-REQ422-20260929/step-02b-mobile-dev.json's quoted aapt dump output directly -- confirmed it supports BOTH clauses (usesCleartextTraffic=0x0 in the manifest, AND the resolved network-security-config resource (res/8G.xml) shows only a base-config with cleartextTrafficPermitted=0x0 and NO domain-config element at all in the release artifact). Not re-executed (no Android build toolchain invoked this step); the existing quote already independently supports both clauses so no re-run was needed.

AC7: audience_scoping_test.dart and transport_policy_test.dart both exercise the bearer-interceptor/transport-policy-interceptor logic via a reimplementation helper (_bearerInterceptorForTest/_transportPolicyInterceptorForTest) because the real interceptors are private closures inside api_client.dart that cannot be imported into a test file. This is flagged in test/specs/REQ-422.md as an observation, not reworked: the underlying decision logic (issuerOf, TransportPolicy.isUrlAllowed) that determines pass/fail IS the real production code under test, and this is a pre-existing accepted pattern in this codebase (same shape in REQ-421's own tests), not a new gap introduced by REQ-422.

AC9: confirmed by direct read of docs/mobile/architecture.md §7 -- contains 'Security hardening before corporate-tier deployment', 'Status: documented now, not implemented in v1 (REQ-422)', names certificate pinning and root/jailbreak detection, both framed as required-before-corporate-tier / not-v1. Guarded against future accidental deletion by test/docs/dated_notes_test.dart.

AC10: git diff 34c827bd..HEAD --stat -- apps/mobile was empty before this step's own edit (only gate-decision commits occurred, no code changes), confirming no regression could have occurred between MOBILE-DEV's quoted analyze/test run and this step. After this step's two added tests: flutter analyze -> 'No issues found! (ran in 12.5s)'. flutter test -> full suite run, '+86: ... All tests passed!' (86, up from the previously-quoted 84 -- the delta is exactly this step's two added self-tests, confirmed by reading the test-name list in the run output).

No implementation changes were needed -- the one gap found was test-only (a missing self-test for an already-correct checker branch), closed directly per this role's mandate to attempt writing the test first.

issues.description: audience_scoping_test.dart and transport_policy_test.dart exercise the real bearer-interceptor/transport-policy-interceptor decision logic (issuerOf, TransportPolicy.isUrlAllowed) but reconstruct the interceptor wiring itself via a test-local helper, since the real interceptor closures are private to lib/api/api_client.dart and cannot be imported directly. Accepted pre-existing pattern (also used in REQ-421's tests); flagged for TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's awareness, not a blocking gap.
